prayer: Prayer: Writ Petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India praying to issue a Writ of Mandamus, directing the respondents to appoint an independent HR and CE Officer/Fit Person to supervise the opening of Hundials on 21.02.2026, to ensure that the opening of Hundials, counting of money and preparation of statement of accounts are done in the presence of villagers with proper videography, to conduct a special audit of the temple accounts for the past three years.
judgment_text:
The Order of the Court was delivered by

Krishnan Ramasamy, J.:— This writ petition has been filed seeking a direction to the respondents to appoint an independent HR & CE Officer/Fit Person to supervise the opening of the hundials on 21.02.2026; to ensure that the opening of the hundials, counting of money and preparation of the statement of accounts are conducted in the presence of villagers with proper videography; and to conduct a special audit of the temple accounts for the past three years.

2. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner would submit that the temple, namely Arulmighu Sri Vinayagar, Sri Perumalsamy, Sri Mariyamman and Sri 18-am Padi Karuppasamy Temple, is an ancient public religious institution, said to be in existence for more than 200 years. According to the petitioner, the temple is managed by members of four communities and the petitioner is one of the devotees. The grievance of the petitioner is that the present Committee members, who have taken over the administration, have failed to follow established customs and transparent practices. Therefore, the petitioner submitted a detailed representation dated 26.11.2025 to the respondents seeking inspection and audit of the temple accounts and appointment of an independent Fit Person to supervise the opening of the hundials on 21.02.2026. However, no action has been taken so far, necessitating the filing of the present writ petition.

3. The learned Special Government Pleader appearing for the respondents would submit that the temple has been in existence for more than 200 years and that the four communities have been carrying on the temple activities and worship by constituting a Committee. It is further submitted that the petitioner, being only a devotee, is attempting to interfere with the affairs of the Committee, though the Committee is functioning without any complaint from the general public. The petitioner, without participating in the temple activities in a proper manner, has unnecessarily approached this Court. Hence, the writ petition is liable to be dismissed.

4. Considering the submissions made on either side, this Court is of the view that the affairs of the temple are being managed by the Committee constituted by the four communities and there is no material placed before this Court to substantiate the allegations of mismanagement or lack of transparency. The petitioner, being a devotee, cannot seek to interfere with the administration of the temple in the absence of any concrete evidence.

5. Accordingly, this Court is not inclined to grant the relief sought for by the petitioner and the writ petition stands dismissed. The petitioner is directed to pay costs of Rs. 5,000/- (Rupees Five Thousand only) to the said temple within a period of one week from today (20.02.2026). If the petitioner has any grievance, it is open to him to approach the temple management in the manner known to law.

6. In the result, the writ petition stands dismissed. There shall be no order as to costs.

7. Registry is directed to list the matter under the caption “For reporting compliance” on 27.02.2026.
